resources.string: NexFlow uses the Accessibility Service for three automation features: capturing a screenshot when a flow\'s screenshot action runs, performing a tap gesture at coordinates you specify when a flow runs a simulated-tap action, and detecting which app is brought to the foreground so your \"App Launched\" triggers can fire. It only reads the package name of the app in front; it does not read screen content, text, or passwords, and it does not send any data to a server. It runs only after you manually enable it.

NexFlow only detects an app being opened. The trigger now fires on launch instead; remove it if that is wrong.
MacroDroid could ignore specific senders or apps. NexFlow can only match, not exclude, so this now reacts to everything the keyword matches.
This fired when a notification was cleared
NexFlow only detects notifications arriving. The trigger now fires on arrival instead; remove it if that is wrong.
The area did not come across
MacroDroid stores the coordinates outside the macro, so only enter/exit was imported. Set the location and radius in the editor, or this trigger will never fire.

Name a variable and the response is stored there, ready to use as {{name}} in later actions. Leave the JSON field empty to store the whole response, or give a dot path such as main.temp or items.0.name to store just that field. The status code is always available as {{__http_status__}} — an error status does not stop the flow, so test it with an If action.
